headline: Approved statement on RSA 32:5i ballot question for school levy and central office caps, with amendments.
summary: The meeting reviewed House Bill 1300, ballot question language for Concord wards, central office functions, and the central office budget. No one spoke during the public comment period. The members then approved a statement on the RSA 32:5i ballot question, with two amendments.
decisions: Approved the statement on the RSA 32:5i ballot question, as amended, by voice vote.
Approved amendment renumbering statement item 3 to 4 and adding a new item 3 on the State’s constitutional obligation, by voice vote.
Approved amendment changing the wording of statement item 4, by voice vote.

decision_titles: Statement on RSA 32:5i ballot question on school caps
Amendment adding new item 3 to statement
plain_text:
Public Hearing 
October 14, 2026 
 
In Attendance: Pamela Walsh-President, Cara Meeker-Vice President, Liz Boucher- Secretary, Jessica 
Campbell (arrived 6:12 pm), Alex Dubois, Brenda Hastings, Barb Higgins, Madeleine Mineau, Sarah 
Sadowski 
 
Administration: Superintendent, Timothy Herbert, Business Administrator, Jack Dunn, Assistant 
Superintendent of Curriculum and Instruction, Kris Gallo 
 
Meeting called to order: 6 pm by Ms. Walsh and roll call attendance was taken by Ms. Boucher 
 
Agenda Items: 
• Call to order: Pamela Walsh, President 
• Ballot Questions 
• Overview of HB1300 
• Functions of Central Office 
• Central Office Budget 
 
Discussion:  
• Dr. Herbert reviewed a PowerPoint presentation that the District created that outlined House 
Bill 1300 “What it does and what it could mean for Concord”. 
• The ballot question language was provided for both Concord Wards 1,2 and Concord Wards 3-
10. 
• The question is two parts to include a District levy cap and a central office cap. Functions of 
the central office staff and what positions are included were presented to the Board. 
• Background of State funding loss and the 3-year adequacy decline were reported 
• FY27 Budget factors were reviewed including FY26 to FY27 expenditure change, staffing 
reductions, and student services costs over 5 years. 
• If budget cap were in place for FY27 budget, what would that look like 
• New obligations by the state that have been placed on school districts was also reviewed  
• See attached PowerPoint slides 
 
Ms. Walsh opened the public comment period at 6:23 pm. Seeing no one in attendance to speak, she 
closed the public hearing at 6:23 pm. 
 
Non-Public Session 
Motion: enter non-public session pursuant to 91-A: 3 II (L) was made by Ms. Walsh at 6:23 pm 
2nd by Ms. Higgins
Executive Committee Meeting Minutes- Date       Page 2 
Roll call vote (9-0) to enter non-public 
 
Ms. Campbell- Yes 
Mr. Dubois- Yes 
Ms. Hastings- Yes 
Ms. Higgins- Yes 
Ms. Meeker- Yes 
Ms. Mineau- Yes 
Ms. Sadowski- Yes 
Ms. Walsh- Yes 
Ms. Boucher- Yes 
 
Motion: come out of non-public session at 6:31 pm 
Made by Ms. Higgins; 2nd Ms. Sadowski  
Voice vote in the affirmative to exit non-public  
 
Motion: Seal the minutes of the non-public session 
Made by Ms. Higgins; 2nd Ms. Hastings 
Roll call vote (9-0) to seal the minutes of non-public session  
 
Ms. Campbell- Yes 
Mr. Dubois- Yes 
Ms. Hastings- Yes 
Ms. Higgins- Yes 
Ms. Meeker- Yes 
Ms. Mineau- Yes 
Ms. Sadowski- Yes 
Ms. Walsh- Yes 
Ms. Boucher- Yes 
 
Motions and Votes:  
 
Motion 1: The Board adopts the following statement of the Concord School Board regarding RSA 
32:5i ballot question.  
1. In Concord, the ballot is critically flawed because it requires voters in Wards 1 and 2 to vote on 
both Merrimack Valley School District and Concord School District budgets despite being legal 
voters of only one of those school districts. The Merrimack Valley School Board has also voted 
to oppose this ballot question. 
 
2. School districts in NH, including Concord, face several costs required by law and are therefore 
beyond their control. These costs often increase more than standard inflation year-over-year, 
such as special education services, transportation, fuel and utilities, collective bargaining 
agreements, and health insurance. At the same time, state and federal funding can decrease
Executive Committee Meeting Minutes- Date       Page 3 
significantly year-over-year. A cap would not change those obligations; it would only reduce 
the revenue available to meet them.  
 
3. The adoption of the caps will enable the State to continue to avoid its constitutional obligation 
to adequately fund education. 
 
4. The assertion in the question that an affirmative vote will not affect classroom instruction or 
school-based services is misleading. Capping the property tax levy for the school district will 
inevitably require cuts that impact classroom instruction and school-based services.  
Statement read by Ms. Mineau.  
 
 
Made by: Ms. Mineau; 2nd Ms. Higgins 
 
Motion 2: Amendment to renumber 3 to 4 and add a new number 3 to read “the adoption of the 
caps will enable the State to continue to avoid its constitutional obligation to adequately fund 
education.” 
 
Made by: Ms. Mineau; 2nd Ms. Walsh 
Voice vote in the affirmative  
 
Motion 3: Amendment to modify language in the new number 4.  
• Change “essentially flat” to “had reduced spending by 0.41%” 
• Change 40 positions to 45 positions 
• Delete “unexpected healthcare assessment” 
• Change “3.5%” to “4%” 
• Include “an additional $6.3 million in budget reductions” 
• Create two sentences by adding a period after necessary and a new sentence to read “Those 
budget cuts would have been severe and significant harm to classroom instruction and 
school-based services would have occurred.” 
 
Made by Ms. Mineau; 2nd by Ms. Walsh 
Voice vote in the affirmative  
 
Voice vote in the affirmation to pass the Board statement with amendments 
 
Ms. Walsh requested that the superintendent distribute the finalized Board statement to media 
outlets tomorrow 10/15. 
 
Adjournment: 
Motion to adjourn made by: Ms. Higgins  
Seconded by: Ms. Meeker 
Voice vote in the affirmative to adjourn the meeting
Executive Committee Meeting Minutes- Date       Page 4 
 
Meeting Adjourned: 6:41 pm 
 
Submitted by: Liz Boucher, Board Secretary
